rationale: Start with a broad gradient to locate the elution window, retain early compounds, and identify poorly resolved pairs. The midpoint temperature leaves room to adjust selectivity in either direction in subsequent injections.

Change only gradient duration to test whether the close pair responds to a shallower slope. The last peak currently elutes at 8.30 min, leaving some room to improve resolution before the time penalty begins.

Shift the starting organic fraction upward while keeping the slope close to injection 2, which fully resolved every pair. This trims low-organic time and should bring the last peak below 10 minutes while retaining adequate early-peak separation.

Narrow the gradient window to make the slope slightly shallower than injection 3 while keeping the same starting composition and temperature. This should lift the critical pair above R = 1.5, with the last peak predicted to remain just below 10 minutes.

Injection 4 already achieves the maximum CRF; now test a shorter fully resolved separation. Raising phi0 while keeping phi1 fixed removes low-organic time and slightly shallows the gradient, potentially preserving the critical-pair resolution while advancing the last peak.

Keep the fully resolved gradient from injection 5 and increase temperature by 5 °C to seek a shorter separation. This isolates temperature’s effect on the critical pair while preserving two established maximum-CRF methods as fallbacks.

Test whether further heating separates the critical pair again after an elution-order reversal, potentially delivering a faster maximum-CRF method. Keep the gradient fixed to isolate temperature selectivity and monitor other pairs for new co-elutions.

Slightly shallow the gradient at 55 °C to improve the newly limiting pair while retaining the temperature-induced separation of the previous critical pair. Injection 7 leaves 1.46 minutes before the time penalty, providing room for this resolution adjustment.

Raise the starting organic fraction to shorten the fully resolved separation from injection 8 while slightly reducing gradient steepness. Monitor early-peak retention and both close middle pairs, since changing the starting composition can alter their selectivity.

Lower phi0 to restore early retention and improve the selectivity lost in injection 9, while using a steeper gradient to shorten late elution. This tests whether a lower starting composition permits a faster fully resolved method at 55 °C.

Shorten only the gradient duration to test whether injection 10’s full resolution can be retained with earlier final elution. The two closest pairs will show whether further speed gains are limited by gradient steepness.

Use a gradient slope between injections 10 and 11, targeting full resolution with the last peak around 7.8 minutes. The narrower endpoint remains above the observed elution window, so the critical pairs should still elute within the gradient.

With maximum CRF already secured, test a substantially faster gradient at 60 °C for an alternative fully resolved elution order. Lowering phi0 protects early retention, while higher temperature and steepness may move the limiting middle pair past its selectivity crossover.

Test whether raising the starting organic fraction separates the middle pair on the reversed-order side of its crossover while shortening the run further. Check the neighboring middle pair and early peaks carefully, since both may lose resolution.

Test a steeper gradient at 60 °C to increase separation of the reversed middle pair, using low phi0 to protect its neighboring pair and early retention. This isolates the slope effect relative to injection 13 and probes a substantially faster separation.

Explore the low-temperature selectivity regime, since the fast 60 °C gradients leave persistent middle-pair overlaps. This broad, moderately steep gradient tests for a different fully resolved ordering while retaining the established maximum-CRF methods as fallbacks.

Test an intermediate temperature below the successful 40 °C regime, avoiding the extensive overlaps observed at 25 °C. The moderately steep gradient probes whether cooler selectivity can resolve the middle cluster in less time than the established methods.

Return to the successful 55 °C regime and lower only phi0 relative to injection 11. This tests whether improved middle-pair selectivity offsets the slightly steeper slope, giving full resolution faster than injection 12.

With maximum CRF and a 7.60-minute fully resolved method established, test a larger resolution margin rather than further speed. A slightly shallower slope than injection 8 should improve its limiting pair while keeping final elution below 10 minutes.

Test a much steeper gradient at 40 °C to see whether the formerly limiting pair separates after an elution-order reversal. This explores a faster selectivity regime while retaining the established maximum-CRF methods as fallbacks.

Trim injection 18’s gradient endpoint while preserving its exact slope of 0.075 organic fraction per minute. All peaks previously eluted below approximately 0.58 organic, so this should preserve maximum CRF while shortening the programmed gradient from 12 to 8 minutes.

Increase the slope slightly from the fastest fully resolved method to test the remaining speed margin at 55 °C. This should advance the last peak, though the middle pair at R = 1.59 may become limiting.

Test a narrower gradient window at the established 40 °C selectivity, aiming to preserve full resolution while removing low-organic time. The cooler temperature should retain the early peaks better than injection 9, while the shallower slope supports separation of the critical middle pair.

Probe the untested 50 °C selectivity regime with a fast gradient, seeking a fully resolved separation shorter than 7.60 minutes. The low starting organic fraction protects early retention; established CRF 1.000 methods remain the fallbacks if the middle cluster overlaps.

Preserve injection 21’s slope through every closely spaced pair, then finish with a hold at 50% organic to shorten the programmed gradient and reduce solvent strength. The isolated last peak may elute later, but its 2.4-minute margin before the time penalty makes this a promising maximum-CRF alternative.
